sentences.text: Mr.Joshi, learned APP waives service of notice of Rule on behalf of respondent State.

1. By way of the present application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the applicant-accused has prayed for anticipatory bail in connection with the FIR being I- C.R.No.11191007230473 of 2023 registered with Bapunagar Police Station, Dist.Ahmedabad for offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 419, 120(b) and 114 of the Indian Penal Code.
2.1 Heard Shri Krunal Agrawal, learned advocate NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/13351/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined appearing for the applicant.
He submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present offence.
The applicant is neither directly nor indirectly involved in the present offence.

He submitted that one of the witnesses viz. Nitin Manishbhai Patel, who is the employee of K.V.Enterprise, has informed the complainant that accused no.9 viz. Mohanlal has duped the complainant for an amount of Rs.85/- Lakhs.
The applicant is not the beneficiary of any amount involved in the present offence.

There is no discovery Vishalbhai Vinodbhai Barad vs State Of Gujarat on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172378781/
1 or recovery of any muddamal articles from the present applicant.

entities.text: Vishalbhai Vinodbhai Barad vs State Of Gujarat on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He, therefore, submitted to allow the present application and enlarge him on anticipatory bail subject to suitable conditions.

2.2 Learned advocate appearing for the applicant submitted that the learned Sessions Court dismissed the application filed by the applicant for anticipatory bail merely on the ground that custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary.

Learned advocate for the applicant, in this regard, relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Ashokkumar vs. Union NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/13351/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined Territory of Chandigarh rendered in Special Leave Petition (Cri.) No.9949 of 2023 wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that mere an assertion on the part of the State while opposing plea in anticipatory bail that custodial interrogation is required would not be sufficient.

entities.text: Ashokkumar vs. Union NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/13351/2024 ORDER
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: State would have to show or indicate more than prima facie why the custodial interrogation of the accused is required for the purpose of investigation.
3. Learned APP Mr.Soaham Joshi appearing for the respondent State has opposed the present application contending that the applicant is actively involved in commission of offence in question.
The applicant had impersonated and introduced himself as some other person and had asked the first informant to deposit an amount of Rs.85/- Lakhs with Angadiya Pedhi.
Thus, there is active involvement of the present applicant in commission of offence in question and, therefore, he prayed to dismiss the present application.

4. Heard learned advocates for the parties and perused the record.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/13351/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined
5. From the record it appears that the present applicant alongwith other co-accused had shown an interest to deal with gold with the first informant.

The role attributed to the present applicant in offence in question is to the effect that applicant herein impersonated himself to be some other person and had asked the first informant to deposit sum of Rs.1,35,00,000/- for purchase of gold from the accused persons.
Pursuant thereto the first informant had deposited the said amount in Angadiyapedhi as directed by the present applicant.

Out of the aforesaid amount, sum of Rs.85/-
Lakhs
has been siphoned- away.
From the record, it appears that present applicant was very much part of conspiracy which had been hatched by the other co-accused persons for commission of offence in question.
Having regard to these facts, no case is made out.
The present application is dismissed.
Rule is discharged.

(M. R. MENGDEY,J) MISHRA AMIT V.
